# @pocket-somm/offer-engine

Aagnostic calculation engine for offers, designed with immutability and precision in mind.

## Core Principles
- **Immutability**: All operations on `Offer` and `OfferItem` return new instances.
- **Precision**: Implements a "No-Drift" calculation engine. Setting an exact target (like `customerPrice` or `gross`) locks that value, preventing rounding errors from derived fields (like `margin`) from drifting the final price.
- **Priority Hierarchy**: When resolving conflicts, the engine prioritizes: `customerPrice` > `gross` > `pricePerBottle` > `margin/discount`.

## Key Components

### OfferItem (`src/OfferItem.ts`)
The foundational unit representing a line item in an offer.
- **Financial Fields**: `price`, `discount`, `margin`, `gross`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `customerPrice`, `glassPrice`.
- **Packaging**: Supports units (e.g., `bottle`, `case_6`, `case_12`).
- **Update Patterns**: Use `.update({ ... })` for single or multiple field changes.
- **Rounding**: `.roundCustomerPrice(step)` and `.roundGlassPrice(step)` for precision adjustments.

### Offer (`src/Offer.ts`)
A collection of `OfferItem`s with aggregated totals.
- **Bulk Operations**: `setMargin`, `setGross`, `setDiscount`, `setQuantity`, `setVatRate`, `setGlassPrice`, `setUnit`.
- **Totals**: Provides `totalNet`, `totalVat`, and `totalGross` for the entire offer.
- **Updates**: Individual item updates via `updateItem(id, fields|fn)`.
- **Status**: `offer.status` (getter, defaults to `'draft'`) and `setStatus(status)`. Valid values:
  `OFFER_STATUSES` (`'draft' | 'sent' | 'accepted'`, type `OfferStatus`).
- **Sort**: `offer.sort` (getter), `setSort({ field, dir } | null)`, and `offer.sortedItems`
  (items in the saved order — insertion order when no sort is set). Persisted on the `data` bag
  like grouping, so an offer's ordering survives a round-trip instead of being a per-session
  consumer preference.

### Sorting (`src/sorting/sortItems.ts`)
`sortItems(items, { field, dir })` — pure, non-mutating ordering. Fields: `name` (by `data.title`,
case-insensitive), `price` (net `pricePerBottle`), `quantity`, `vintage` (falls back to `data.year`).
Direction: `'asc' | 'desc'`. `DEFAULT_SORT` is `{ field: 'price', dir: 'asc' }`. An unknown field is a
deliberate no-op (returns the items in their existing order) so a stale persisted sort can never
throw or drop items.

### Menus (`offer.menus`)
An offer holds **`menus: readonly any[]`** — opaque menu objects the engine never inspects (pairing
logic lives in the consumer app). Mutate immutably with `setMenus(menus)`, `addMenu(menu)`,
`removeMenu(menuId)` (matches on `menu.id`). Back-compat during the single→multi migration:
- `offer.menu` is a **getter** returning `menus[0] ?? null` (prototype getter, so `{ ...offer }` spreads
  `menus`, never a stale `menu`).
- `setMenu(menu)` is a shim → `setMenus(menu ? [menu] : [])`.
- The constructor accepts a legacy single `menu` and wraps it into `menus`; `menus` wins if both given.
- `toJSON()` writes `menus` **and** mirrors the first under `menu` for readers still on the old shape.

### Convention: the `data` bag (`offer.data` / `item.data`)
Both `Offer` and `OfferItem` carry a free-form `data: Record<string, any>` that the constructor
preserves verbatim across every immutable operation. It's the home for consumer-owned, non-financial
fields the engine doesn't model — so a feature can be added **without** widening the typed config.
- The engine itself uses it for `data.grouping` (see `setGrouping`/custom categories) and `data.status`.
- Consumer apps store their own keys here too (e.g. `data.documents`). Write via the
  constructor-spread pattern: `new Offer({ ...offer, data: { ...offer.data, myField } })`.
- `OfferItem.data` holds the original wine object (`imgUrl`, `title`, region, etc.).

### Convention: `toSummary()` and `toJSON().summary`
`toSummary()` returns a compact `OfferSummary` for list/index views that shouldn't load every item:
- `thumbnails` — flat `{imgUrl,title}[]`, first 8 items (`SUMMARY_THUMBNAIL_LIMIT`).
- `groups` — the same wines grouped **the way the offer itself is grouped**:
  `{ value, label?, count, thumbnails }[]`. Each group is capped at 3 thumbnails
  (`SUMMARY_GROUP_THUMBNAIL_LIMIT`) while `count` reports the group's **true** size, so a list row can
  render a "+N" tile. `label` is set only for custom categories; built-in `type`/`country` groups
  expose a `value` key the consumer localizes itself. Empty groups are omitted.
- `groupingMode` — the mode `groups` was built with.
- `wineCount`, `status`.
- `menuTitles` — titles of all attached menus in order (untitled menus omitted); `[]` when none.

Item order (flat and within groups) follows the offer's saved `sort`, or insertion order when unset.

**Strategy grouping is previewed as `type`.** A saved strategy's definition (categories + filter
rules) lives in the *consumer app*, not on the offer — `groupItems` needs it passed in via
`options.savedStrategies`, which `toSummary()` has no access to. Manual (`custom`) grouping is fully
self-contained on `offer.data.grouping` and IS honoured, as are `type`/`country`.

`toJSON()` embeds the summary as `summary`, a **top-level sibling of `items`/`totals`** (not nested
under `data`). Because it's part of `toJSON()`, it's recomputed on every serialization and can't
drift. The save envelope is `{ data: offer.toJSON() }`, so a list endpoint surfaces the brief payload
by reading `record.data.summary`; the status lives one level deeper at `record.data.data.status`.
NOTE: the summary is written at save time — offers stored before a summary-shape change keep the old
shape until they're next saved.

### Line identity: `item.lineId`
Every `OfferItem` carries a durable `lineId` (defaults to `id`; stored blobs without it load as
`lineId === id`). Unlike `id` — which `swapItem()` replaces and `removeItems()` drops — `lineId` is
carried onto a swap's replacement item, so a reference to "this slot in the offer" survives rounds
of negotiation. An explicit `lineId` in a swap config wins (that's how swap-undo restores identity).

### Negotiation (`src/negotiation/`, stored at `offer.data.negotiation`)
Two-way change negotiation on a live offer. `NegotiationState`: `state` (`'open'|'accepted'`),
`turn` (`'seller'|'buyer'`), append-only `versions` (one per transmission: sender, sentAt, frozen
display `log`, and a compact `baseline` of the lines as transmitted), the live round's `requests`,
and `unpromptedNotes` (seller notes keyed by lineId).
- **Outcomes are derived, never stored.** `resolveRequest(request, offer)` returns
  `{ outcome: 'open'|'done'|'changed'|'declined', label, params }` — label is an i18n token
  (`doneAsAsked`, `setToInstead`, `cutToInstead`, `swappedFor`, `droppedNoReplacement`,
  `removedInstead`, `removed`, `added`, `answered`, `declined`, plus the cross-dimension
  `volumeInstead`, `swappedInstead`, `priceInstead`). Editing the wine list by hand settles a
  request identically to any sidebar shortcut. The only stored resolution state:
  `declined`, `answerNote`, `answeredFreeText` (for free-text asks with nothing to derive from).
- **Cross-dimension answers never vanish.** A request is compared to the round-opening baseline
  across ALL dimensions (quantity, unit, wine identity, price). Answering an ask with a *different*
  kind of change is reported as `changed` on the request itself — e.g. a `replace` the seller
  answers by cutting the volume → `changed`/`volumeInstead` (not a stuck `open`). This includes a
  `note` (a question) answered *by acting* — swapping the noted wine settles the note and names the
  swap, rather than leaving it stuck open. The requested dimension wins when it's actually satisfied.
- **Baseline carries `imgUrl`.** Each baseline line stores the wine's thumbnail, so a consumer can
  keep showing the wine a request was *about* even after that line is swapped for a different wine.
- **Units are tracked.** A `quantity` request carries `fromUnit`/`toUnit` (`toUnit` defaults to the
  line's current unit), so "10 bottles → 10 cases" is expressible; `done` requires both the
  quantity AND unit to match. `params` on quantity outcomes is `{ qty, unit }`.
- **Unprompted changes are derived too**: `deriveUnpromptedChanges(offer)` diffs current items vs
  the latest version's baseline (quantity/price/swap/add/remove), excluding edits a live request
  explains. Reverting the edit removes the entry.
- **Flow methods on `Offer`** (immutable, timestamps caller-supplied — the engine never reads the
  clock): `sendVersion({ senderName, sentAt, log })` (seller; also sets status `'sent'`),
  `submitRequests({ requests, senderName, sentAt })` (buyer; stamps `from` off current lines),
  `declineRequest/undeclineRequest(id)`, `setRequestAnswer(id, note)`,
  `markFreeTextAnswered(id)`, `setUnpromptedNote(lineId, note)`, `acceptNegotiation()`.
- Helpers: `resolveRequests`, `countOpenRequests`, `itemByLineId`, `latestBaseline`.
- `toSummary()` embeds `negotiation: { state, turn, openCount, versionCount }` once shared — list
  rows badge "Your move" / "Their move" / "Approved" without loading items.
- Versions are **a record, not a snapshot**: baselines exist only to derive deltas/unprompted
  changes for the following round; there is no restore and no historical rendering.

## Usage for Agents
- Always use the `update` methods rather than creating new objects from scratch if you want to preserve the "lock" on explicit targets.
- The `dist/` directory is built using `tsup`. Run `npm run build` after changes.
- Verification is done via `vitest`. Run `npm test`.
